title: This is that Devadatta
hookLine: an old teaching manual explains tat tvam asi with a John Doe
carry: advaita: under every label, one awareness
tomorrow: something lives in the earth, and the earth doesn't know it. how?
last: ASKING AGAIN IS HOW IT GOES ON.

lines: HOW IS IT THE SAME PERSON?
cards: An airport gate. Someone in line turns around, and the face takes a second. A teacher from third grade?
Grayer now, different glasses, a different city, years later. Then it clicks, and the sentence comes out by itself: that's her. Nobody hearing it is confused.
Advaita teachers reach for exactly this kind of sentence to explain tat tvam asi. But how can then-her and now-her be one person?

teach.b: Back in the Chandogya, Uddalaka told his son Shvetaketu, again and again: that you are.
Centuries later, the Advaita school, the school Shankara taught, explained the line with an example from a teaching manual called the Vedantasara. Its sentence is: this is that Devadatta.
Devadatta is a stock name in old Sanskrit examples, a bit like John Doe. Here's the logic, in paraphrase.
That Devadatta means the man as he was, then, there. This Devadatta means the man as he is, now, here. Then and now can't both be true of him at once.

So you quietly set aside the time and the place, and keep the person. Now try it on tat tvam asi. In the Advaita reading, that points to awareness in the language of the vast and the far: knowing everything, beyond sight.
You points to awareness in the language of the small and the near: this body, this mind, this one life. As labels, they clash.

teach.h: SET ASIDE THE LABELS, BOTH SIDES.
teach.b: So both sets of labels are set aside, and what's left is the one awareness both words pointed at. Notice what this reading doesn't say. It doesn't say your ego is God.
The little labels of you go just as firmly as the grand labels of that.
What remains isn't a bigger me. In this school's reading, it's awareness without the labels, and that awareness, the atman, is not other than Brahman. That is Advaita's big teaching.
Other schools hear the line differently, and the next two days give them their turn.

how: In Advaita study, students learn the Vedantasara's 'this is that Devadatta' as a standard way of explaining how tat tvam asi points past the labels of both words.

o: that person over there is your twin
that you are: the labels drop, one awareness stays
you are your job, your name and your role

games.q: a classmate posts 'tat tvam asi = i'm literally God, bow down 👑'. what does the Advaita reading say about that?
o: the labels of 'you' go too; what's left isn't a bigger me.
exactly right: Advaita says your personality is God.
Advaita says the line is about someone far away, not you.
games.why: the Vedantasara sets aside the small labels of 'you' just as firmly as the grand ones of 'that'. what remains, in this reading, is awareness without labels.

practice: Write your name on a scrap of paper, and under it two or three labels you carry: a role, a job, a nickname. Read each one, then set the pen down and let the labels stay there on the page.
Rest a while in the plain awareness that read them.

wordCard.voice: Tat tvam asi, read the Advaita way: set the labels aside on both sides, and one awareness is left.

carryVoice: Keep this one: under every label, one awareness. This is that Devadatta, older now and the very same. See you tomorrow.
